title: Frontier Topics Map
subtitle: What Is Production vs Research (and How to Tell)
content:
🎯 What You'll Be Able to Do

  • Separate production-ready techniques from research bets
  • Evaluate a frontier claim with a 5-minute checklist
  • Know where the quantum-AI material lives and when to read it

Before you start: complete Lesson 15 (LLM Evaluation). This lesson is judgment, not code.

🗺️ The Map

TechniqueStatusEvidence bar
RAG + eval (Lessons 13, 15)ProductionGolden set + faithfulness on your data
Tool-calling agents (Lessons 16, 18)Production, with guardrailsRed-team set + traces + max-iterations bound
Small-model fine-tuning / QLoRA (Lesson 14)Production, narrowBase-vs-tuned on held-out data + forgetting check
Quantum ML advantageResearchProblem-specific paper + reproduction; see quantum-course/

Rule of thumb: if nobody can show you a held-out eval on data shaped like yours, it is research — interesting, worth tracking, not worth betting a launch on.

🔍 The 5-Minute Claim Checklist

  1. What exactly improved, on what dataset? "Exponential speedup" with no problem named is hype (remember the AI Winters, Lesson 1).
  2. Versus what baseline? A new method beating a weak baseline proves nothing.
  3. Held-out? Tuned-on-golden numbers are leakage, not evidence (Lessons 15, 19-21).
  4. Cost included? Latency, hardware, and maintenance count (Lesson 7).
  5. Who reproduces it? One lab's demo vs independent replication.

⚫️ Quantum-AI Lives Next Door

The full quantum lesson (qubits → Qiskit 1.x → kernels → caveats) moved to quantum-course/ with per-claim citations (CITATIONS.md). Read it after Lessons 3 + 5, when you want research breadth — not as a job skill.

Honest summary: quantum ML is theoretically rich and practically unproven for ML advantage. Track it; don't plan around it.

questions.question: Which of these is production-ready today with the right guardrails?

options.text: RAG with golden-set eval, or tool-calling agents with red-teaming + traces
Quantum ML advantage on general workloads
Any method with a vendor benchmark slide

questions.explanation: RAG, guarded agents, and narrow fine-tuning ship today when measured; quantum advantage remains research.

questions.question: A vendor claims exponential speedup on all ML workloads. Best response?

options.text: Ask which problems, versus which baseline, on held-out data — and check Lesson 1's AI Winters
Ask for a bigger benchmark number

questions.explanation: Problem-specific evidence + baseline + held-out eval. Hype cycles (AI Winters) are the historical warning.

questions.question: A frontier demo reports 99% on its eval set — tuned on the same set. What is this?

options.text: Eval leakage; the number is not evidence

questions.explanation: Tuning on the reporting set leaks; keep tuning and reporting sets disjoint (Lessons 15, 19-21).

questions.question: First step before adopting a frontier technique in production?

options.text: Reproduce it on your data and measure against your current baseline, cost included

questions.explanation: Your data + your baseline + cost (latency/hardware/maintenance) is the only adoption test that matters.

questions.question: How is the quantum-AI material positioned in this course?

options.text: Standalone research track (quantum-course/): theoretical/contested, read after Lessons 3 + 5
Core hiring skill, required for all tracks

questions.explanation: Quantum lives next door as cited research material — track it, don't plan launches around it.
